data.name: About_WhatIsText
data.value: A civic platform built on official Knesset data. We show which bills are under discussion right now, what stage they are at, who submitted them and what they actually mean. While a bill is still being discussed it can be influenced; by the time it makes the news it is usually too late.

data.name: About_NotOfficialText
data.value: This is not the official Knesset website and is not affiliated with it. The official source is knesset.gov.il, and we link to it from every bill page. Nor is this legal advice: the analysis helps you understand the gist, but decisions about your rights should rest on the primary source and, where needed, a lawyer.

data.name: About_DataText
data.value: Bills, members, factions and the body of laws in force come from the Knesset's official open API and update automatically. The indirect-amendment marking — when a law on one subject changes a law on another — is also assigned by the Knesset itself; we merely bring it into view.

data.name: About_AiText
data.value: The analysis currently runs on demo data — a real model is not connected yet, and the cards are marked accordingly. Once it is, the analysis will be bound by symmetry rules: arguments from all sides, facts kept separate from inferences, and no presenting a guess as established.

data.name: Priv_CollectText
data.value: Your email address and password — the password only as an irreversible hash, never in plain text. A display name if you set one: registration does not ask for it, so it starts out empty. Interface language and notification mode. Your subscriptions: the words, MKs and bills you follow. A delivery address for notifications if you add one — it is stored separately from your sign-in address. Your positions on bills, your comments, your civic initiatives and the signatures you give them.

data.name: Priv_PublicText
data.value: Comments, civic initiatives and their signatures are visible to every visitor, including those who are not registered. A comment is signed with the display name you chose; without one it shows a neutral "Member" — your email address never appears in the signature. Your individual position on a bill is not shown to others: it only enters the shared counter as a number.

data.name: Priv_PoliticalText
data.value: Marking a bill "for", "against" or "undecided" is information about your political views, and we treat it as such. It is stored against your account because otherwise we could not show you your own vote or let you change it. Publicly it appears only as an aggregate count and percentage, with no names. Deleting your account deletes it too.

data.name: Priv_ThirdText
data.value: The site runs on Render hosting with a Supabase database; both are located in Frankfurt, in the European Union. Page fonts are loaded from Google Fonts servers, so opening any page reveals your IP address and browser details to Google — this happens before any registration. Share buttons are ordinary links to social networks: until you click one, those services learn nothing about you. Knesset data comes from its open API, which receives only our request and nothing about visitors. The language model for analysing bills is not connected yet; no data is sent to it.

data.name: Priv_CookiesText
data.value: Three kinds: a sign-in cookie so you do not have to log in on every page; a cookie holding your chosen language; and a technical token protecting forms against request forgery. There is no analytics, no visitor counter and no advertising tracker on this site.

data.name: Priv_RetentionText
data.value: Notifications you have read are deleted automatically after 30 days. Everything else is kept while your account exists. A comment can be deleted at any time — there is a delete button next to it.

data.name: Priv_RightsText
data.value: You can download your data and delete your account yourself, without contacting us. Deletion is irreversible: subscriptions, positions on bills and comments go with the account.

data.name: Priv_ContactText
data.value: The site's source code is open, and this page was written from it: every statement here can be checked against the code. If anything about data handling changes, this page changes too — the update date is at the top.
